content.content: # Date & time utilities: missing duration format, and the current output has drifted Our shared date & time utilities cover relative time, absolute time/date, and combined date-and-time/range formatting. Two things need fixing. ## 1. Add a duration format A duration format shows the absolute length of time (e.g. 2 seconds, 1 hour 30 minutes) — unlike relative time (e.g. "1 hour ago"). Add it alongside the existing formatters, following their conventions: an options object with `locale` and `style`, a sensible default style, exposed through the same public surface consumers already import from. Wrap the platform's native [`Intl.DurationFormat`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Intl/DurationFormat). For 1 hour, 23 minutes and 45 seconds in `en-US`, the expected outputs are: | style | output | | --- | --- | | (default) | 1h 23m 45s | | long | 1 hour, 23 minutes, 45 seconds | | short | 1 hr, 23 min, 45 sec | | narrow | 1h 23m 45s | | digital | 1:23:45 | The attached design-guidance table defines these conventions (reference output, permitted variants, default per format) for the existing formatters — it has no Duration row yet; that's the gap this fills. ## 2. Fix the drift from that guidance Our internal demo pages, rendered against the current code, show several formatters — across more than one utility — no longer matching that guidance. The demos are self-checking: each row's caption states its own call/config, and the same value is shown across several locales side by side — so wrong output always sits next to a caption or locale column that shows what's right. Done when the duration format matches the table above, and everything in the demo screenshots renders the way the guidance table and each row's caption say it should.

FROM node:24-bookworm

 && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

WORKDIR /app

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# READ THIS BEFORE FLAGGING environment/assets/bugs/bug_01.patch
#
# bug_01.patch is the injected-regression diff: base commit -> the rendering
# regressions in the date/time formatters and the overflow handler. It is the
# exact inverse of the corresponding hunks of solution/fix.patch. That is what
# a bug-injection patch IS, and it is why it must never reach the agent.
#
# It is deliberately absent from ASSET_MANIFEST.json / evidence_bundle.json /
# instruction.md: those files describe the visual evidence the agent is pointed
# at, and documenting the regression diff there would hand over the golden fix
# in plaintext. A checker that treats every file under environment/assets/ as a
# poster will flag it as "undocumented"; that flag is expected and is a false
# positive.
#
# The file is used at BUILD time only, in two places, and removed in both:
#   1. `COPY assets/ /tmp/ctx/` stages it OUTSIDE /app. The RUN below applies it
#      and ends with `rm -rf /tmp/ctx` in the same layer.
#   2. `COPY assets/ /app/.harbor_assets/` (further down) necessarily brings
#      assets/bugs/ along with the posters; the RUN straight after deletes it
#      and ASSERTS both that the directory is gone and that no *.patch survives
#      anywhere beneath /app/.harbor_assets - the build fails otherwise.
# The agent also runs with network_mode = "no-network" against a tree whose
# .git history was stripped, so the diff cannot be recovered from anywhere else.
# Verify on the built image:
#   docker run --rm <image> ls /app/.harbor_assets/
#   docker run --rm <image> find / -name '*.patch' -not -path '/proc/*' -not -path '*/node_modules/*'
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Fetch EXACTLY the base commit by SHA (depth 1) - time-invariant regardless of
# how far the default branch has moved since. Apply the bundled regressions
# BEFORE the harbor_base snapshot, so they are part of the tree the agent starts
# from. Then strip .git and re-init a single base commit + immutable tag so the
# verifier can reset test files with `git checkout harbor_base --` (anti-cheat:
# the agent cannot inspect the fix PR or future history).
#
# The guards are load-bearing: a bare `for ... done` returns the status of its
# last command, so without them a patch that failed to apply would still produce
# an image - one where the f2p already pass on the untouched base and nop no
# longer scores 0.
RUN set -eu \
 && test -d /tmp/ctx/bugs \
    || { echo "FATAL: environment/assets/bugs/ is missing from the build context"; exit 1; } \
 && ls /tmp/ctx/bugs/*.patch >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    || { echo "FATAL: no .patch files in environment/assets/bugs/"; exit 1; } \
 && git init -q /app \
 && git -C /app remote add origin https://github.com/carbon-design-system/carbon.git \
 && git -C /app fetch --depth 1 origin 217994d634aaffb2754b73e6dc85bcaaa629e8ff \
 && git -C /app checkout FETCH_HEAD \
 && for p in /tmp/ctx/bugs/*.patch; do \
      echo "applying regression $p"; \
      git -C /app apply "$p" || patch -p1 -d /app < "$p" \
        || { echo "FATAL: could not apply $p"; exit 1; }; \
    done \
 && rm -rf /tmp/ctx \
 && rm -rf /app/.git \
 && git -C /app init -q \
 && git -C /app -c user.email=h@l -c user.name=h add -A \
 && git -C /app -c user.email=h@l -c user.name=h commit -q -m base \
 && git -C /app tag harbor_base

# Match this base commit's packageManager (yarn@4.10.3 via corepack) exactly.
# Focus only the root package + this task's own package (@carbon/utilities) +
# the shared jest/babel infra packages. jest, babel-jest, jest-junit and
# @testing-library/jest-dom are the repo's own root devDependencies (its normal
# development install), not test-only tooling added for grading - nothing is
# fetched at verify time.
ENV PUPPETEER_SKIP_DOWNLOAD=true
RUN corepack enable && yarn workspaces focus carbon @carbon/utilities @carbon/styles @carbon/test-utils jest-config-carbon

# Visual evidence - readable by the agent at /app/.harbor_assets/.
# tests/ and solution/ are supplied by the harness at verify time - NOT baked in.
RUN mkdir -p /logs /app/.harbor_assets
COPY assets/ /app/.harbor_assets/

# Delete the regression diffs from the agent-visible directory, then ASSERT none
# survived. The two `test` calls fail the build if the answer key is ever still
# reachable, so the guarantee cannot rot silently if the asset layout changes.
RUN rm -rf /app/.harbor_assets/bugs \
 && test ! -e /app/.harbor_assets/bugs \
 && test -z "$(find /app/.harbor_assets -name '*.patch' -print -quit)"

CMD ["bash"]

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Oracle solution: apply the human developer's fix (source files only; no test files).
set -euxo pipefail
cd /app

apply_if_nonempty() {
  local p="$1"
  if [ ! -f "$p" ] || ! grep -q '[^[:space:]]' "$p"; then
    return 0
  fi

  if ! git apply "$p" 2>/dev/null; then
    # `patch` is kept as a whitespace-tolerant fallback, but unlike `git apply`
    # it is NOT atomic: it can apply some hunks and reject others, leaving a
    # half-fixed tree whose reward is indistinguishable from a genuine failure.
    # The post-condition below is what actually decides success.
    patch -p1 --forward < "$p" || true
  fi

  # `git apply --reverse --check` succeeds only when EVERY hunk is already
  # present, so it is an exact test for "the patch applied completely".
  if ! git apply --reverse --check "$p" 2>/dev/null; then
    set +x
    echo "FATAL: $p did not apply completely."
    echo "The working tree does not match the state this patch expects."
    echo "fix.patch and environment/assets/bugs/*.patch are a matched pair, regenerated"
    echo "together: the bug patch's 'index a..b' must mirror the fix patch's 'index b..a'"
    echo "for the same file. If only one was synced they disagree about harbor_base."
    echo "Sync the stale one, rebuilding the image only if it is the bug patch that moved."
    find /app -name '*.rej' -print 2>/dev/null || true
    exit 1
  fi
}

apply_if_nonempty /solution/fix.patch
echo "Applied fix.patch."

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Behavioral verifier for carbon-design-system__carbon-22307-mm.
#
# Runs four jest test files from one JUnit report:
#   duration-test.js          f2p  - the new duration format (upstream PR tests +
#                                    a synthetic index-wiring check)
#   defaults-test.js          f2p  - documented conventions of the existing
#                                    formatters: default-option output and locale
#                                    pass-through (all expectations derived from
#                                    Intl at runtime, never hardcoded)
#   overflow-behavior-test.js f2p  - the overflow handler's contract when a
#                                    container overflows
#   relative-test.js          p2p  - pre-existing, untouched regression pool
#   absolute-test.js          p2p  - pre-existing, untouched regression pool
# NEVER greps source for the fix - it runs the tests.
set -uo pipefail
mkdir -p /logs/verifier
STDOUT_LOG=/logs/verifier/test-stdout.txt
STDERR_LOG=/logs/verifier/test-stderr.txt
REPORT=/logs/verifier/report.xml
: > "$STDOUT_LOG"; : > "$STDERR_LOG"

ensure_reward() { [ -f /logs/verifier/reward.txt ] || echo 0 > /logs/verifier/reward.txt; }
trap ensure_reward EXIT

cd /app || { echo "no /app" | tee -a "$STDERR_LOG"; exit 1; }

# ── Step 1: restore any test paths the agent may have edited ─────────────────
# Paths come from the `diff --git` headers, not `+++ b/`: the latter is absent
# for binary, renamed and deleted entries. New-file paths (absent from
# harbor_base) fall through to `rm -f`, so vandalized copies are removed before
# test.patch recreates them.
echo "== restoring test files to harbor_base ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
_patch_paths=$(
  { sed -n 's#^diff --git a/\(.*\) b/.*#\1#p' /tests/test.patch
    sed -n 's#^diff --git a/.* b/\(.*\)#\1#p' /tests/test.patch
  } | sort -u )
for _p in $_patch_paths; do
  git -C /app checkout harbor_base -- "$_p" 2>/dev/null || rm -f "/app/$_p" 2>/dev/null || true
  rm -f "/app/$_p.orig" "/app/$_p.rej" 2>/dev/null || true
done
# The two p2p pools are pre-existing files NOT in test.patch, so they are
# restored explicitly - otherwise an agent could edit them to force their
# regression tests to trivially pass regardless of the real fix.
for _p in packages/utilities/src/dateTimeFormat/relative-test.js \
          packages/utilities/src/dateTimeFormat/absolute-test.js; do
  git -C /app checkout harbor_base -- "$_p" 2>/dev/null || true
  rm -f "/app/$_p.orig" "/app/$_p.rej" 2>/dev/null || true
done

echo "== applying test.patch ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
git apply --binary /tests/test.patch 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
  || git apply /tests/test.patch 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
  || patch -p1 -i /tests/test.patch 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
  || { echo "ERROR: could not apply test.patch" | tee -a "$STDERR_LOG"; exit 1; }

echo "== creating jest config ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
# Everything jest needs (jest, babel-jest, jest-junit, @testing-library/jest-dom,
# the babel presets) is a root devDependency of the repo itself, installed into
# the image by its normal `yarn workspaces focus` - no test-only tooling is
# fetched at verify time. moduleFileExtensions lists 'tsx' before 'ts' so an
# off-file alternative fix that shadows a .ts module with a .tsx sibling
# resolves correctly.
cat > /tmp/jest-verifier.config.cjs << 'JESTEOF'
module.exports = {
  rootDir: '/app',
  testEnvironment: 'jsdom',
  setupFilesAfterEnv: ['/app/node_modules/@testing-library/jest-dom'],
  testMatch: [
    '<rootDir>/packages/utilities/src/dateTimeFormat/duration-test.js',
    '<rootDir>/packages/utilities/src/dateTimeFormat/defaults-test.js',
    '<rootDir>/packages/utilities/src/dateTimeFormat/relative-test.js',
    '<rootDir>/packages/utilities/src/dateTimeFormat/absolute-test.js',
    '<rootDir>/packages/utilities/src/overflowHandler/overflow-behavior-test.js',
  ],
  transform: {
    '^.+\\.(mjs|cjs|js|jsx|ts|tsx)$': ['babel-jest', {
      presets: [
        ['@babel/preset-env', { targets: { node: 'current' } }],
        '@babel/preset-typescript',
      ],
      plugins: [
        '@babel/plugin-proposal-export-default-from',
        '@babel/plugin-transform-class-properties',
        '@babel/plugin-transform-export-namespace-from',
      ],
    }],
  },
  reporters: ['default', 'jest-junit'],
  moduleFileExtensions: ['tsx', 'ts', 'js', 'jsx', 'json', 'node'],
  transformIgnorePatterns: [
    '/node_modules/(?!lodash-es|nanoid|chalk)',
  ],
};
JESTEOF

echo "== running f2p + p2p tests ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
JEST_JUNIT_OUTPUT_DIR=/logs/verifier \
JEST_JUNIT_OUTPUT_NAME=report.xml \
BABEL_ENV=test \
  ./node_modules/.bin/jest \
  --config /tmp/jest-verifier.config.cjs \
  --no-coverage --forceExit --runInBand \
  >>"$STDOUT_LOG" 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
  || echo "(tests exited non-zero; parsing report)" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"

echo "== computing reward ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
# This task ships no rubric layer: every requirement is covered by behavioural
# tests, so tests/rubrics.json and tests/judge.py are both intentionally absent.
# The call below is guarded on rubrics.json rather than deleted: the wiring
# stays visible and correct, while the branch cannot fire in a bundle that
# ships no rubric file. Guarding on the rubric file (not on judge.py) makes
# adding a rubric layer later a pure addition.
RUBRIC=""
if [ -f /tests/rubrics.json ]; then
  RUBRIC=$(python3 /tests/judge.py --rubrics /tests/rubrics.json --repo /app \
             2>/logs/verifier/judge.log || echo "")
fi

# verifier.py always accepts --rubric; an empty or missing path records
# rubric_passed = -1 ("not graded"), which never withholds a reward - only an
# explicit 0 does.
python3 /tests/verifier.py --rubric "${RUBRIC:-}" 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
echo "reward=$(cat /logs/verifier/reward.txt 2>/dev/null)" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"

Verifier for carbon-design-system__carbon-22307-mm.

Reads the JUnit XML report produced by test.sh (jest-junit) and computes the
reward. NEVER inspects candidate source - reward derives solely from the test
report.

Reward domain is pass/fail only:
  1.0 - every f2p passes AND every p2p passes AND the rubric did not fail.
  0.0 - anything else. How close a partial fix got is carried by the counts.
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import re
import sys
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

CONF = json.load(open('/tests/config.json'))
F2P = CONF['f2p']
P2P = CONF['p2p']
REPORT = '/logs/verifier/report.xml'   # keep in sync with test.sh
REWARD_TXT = '/logs/verifier/reward.txt'
REWARD_JSON = '/logs/verifier/reward.json'

RUBRIC_NOT_GRADED = -1


def parse_args():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument(
        '--rubric',
        default=None,
        help='Optional path to a rubric verdict file. Absent => rubric_passed = -1.',
    )
    args, _unknown = parser.parse_known_args()
    return args


def load_results():
    """Return {classname::name: 'pass'|'fail'|'skip'} from JUnit XML."""
    results = {}
    if not os.path.exists(REPORT):
        return results
    try:
        tree = ET.parse(REPORT)
    except ET.ParseError as e:
        print(f'[verifier] XML parse error: {e}', file=sys.stderr)
        return results
    for tc in tree.iter('testcase'):
        name = f"{tc.get('classname', '')}::{tc.get('name', '')}".strip(':')
        failed = any(c.tag in ('failure', 'error') for c in tc)
        skipped = any(c.tag == 'skipped' for c in tc)
        results[name] = 'skip' if skipped else ('fail' if failed else 'pass')
    return results


def matched(idents, results):
    """Match each configured identifier against reported test names (substring)."""
    out = {}
    for ident in idents:
        hit = next(
            (v for k, v in results.items()
             if ident in k or re.search(re.escape(ident), k)),
            None,
        )
        out[ident] = hit or 'missing'
    return out


def load_rubric(path):
    """Return 1 (passed), 0 (failed) or -1 (not graded)."""
    if not path or not os.path.exists(path):
        return RUBRIC_NOT_GRADED
    try:
        with open(path) as fh:
            data = json.load(fh)
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        return RUBRIC_NOT_GRADED
    if isinstance(data, bool):
        return int(data)
    if isinstance(data, dict):
        for key in ('rubric_passed', 'rubric_pass', 'passed', 'pass'):
            if key in data and isinstance(data[key], (bool, int, float)):
                return int(data[key])
    return RUBRIC_NOT_GRADED


def main():
    args = parse_args()
    r = load_results()
    f2p = matched(F2P, r)
    p2p = matched(P2P, r)

    f2p_passed = sum(1 for v in f2p.values() if v == 'pass')
    p2p_passed = sum(1 for v in p2p.values() if v == 'pass')

    all_f2p = len(F2P) > 0 and f2p_passed == len(F2P)
    all_p2p = p2p_passed == len(P2P)

    rubric_passed = load_rubric(args.rubric)
    # "Not graded" (-1) must never withhold a reward; only an explicit 0 does.
    rubric_ok = rubric_passed != 0

    tests_ok = all_f2p and all_p2p
    reward = 1.0 if (tests_ok and rubric_ok) else 0.0

    # reward.json stays flat and numeric. `tests_passed` is a binary 0/1 flag,
    # not a count -- the counts live in the f2p_*/p2p_* fields.
    payload = {
        'reward': reward,
        'tests_passed': 1 if tests_ok else 0,
        'f2p_passed': f2p_passed,
        'f2p_total': len(F2P),
        'p2p_passed': p2p_passed,
        'p2p_total': len(P2P),
        'rubric_passed': rubric_passed,
    }
    # Per-test scalars let a nop run prove no f2p is inert (passes with no fix).
    for ident, v in f2p.items():
        payload[f'f2p::{ident}'] = 1.0 if v == 'pass' else 0.0
    for ident, v in p2p.items():
        payload[f'p2p::{ident}'] = 1.0 if v == 'pass' else 0.0

    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(REWARD_TXT), exist_ok=True)
    with open(REWARD_TXT, 'w') as fh:
        fh.write(str(reward))
    with open(REWARD_JSON, 'w') as fh:
        json.dump(payload, fh)

    print(json.dumps({**payload, 'f2p': f2p, 'p2p': p2p,
                      'testcases_in_report': len(r)}))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
